figure.name: J. P. Morgan
figure.era: Gilded Age finance, railroads, steel, and panic management (1870-1913)
figure.role: Financier and banker associated with railroad reorganization, industrial consolidation, U.S. Steel, the Money Trust debate, and the Panic of 1907.
figure.hook: Morgan = finance capital, railroads, steel, panic control, and private banking power.
whyHere: Morgan belongs here because American capitalism was built not only by inventors and factories, but by bankers who organized railroads, steel, debt, mergers, and credit.
He matters because the Panic of 1907 shows private finance acting like an emergency central bank before the Federal Reserve existed.
figure.cleanIdea: Finance capital can organize industry, rescue markets, and concentrate enough private power that democracy has to ask who controls credit.

ideas.title: Finance Capital
ideas.plainDefinition: Finance capital is power organized through banks, credit, securities, debt, mergers, investment, and control over access to money.
ideas.context: In the Morgan path, finance capital reorganizes railroads, consolidates industry, and manages crisis.
ideas.whyMatters: Finance capital matters because controlling credit can mean controlling the terms under which factories, railroads, governments, and workers survive.

ideas.title: Money Trust
ideas.plainDefinition: Money Trust is a political term for concentrated control over banking, credit, securities, and corporate finance by a small financial elite.
ideas.context: In the Morgan path, the Money Trust debate asks whether private bankers governed too much of the economy.
ideas.whyMatters: Money Trust matters because democracy cannot ignore who controls credit, mergers, panic response, and investment access.

ideas.title: Panic Management
ideas.plainDefinition: Panic management is the emergency response to financial runs, credit freezes, market crashes, and confidence crises.
ideas.context: In the Morgan path, panic management shows private banking power stepping into a role later associated with public central banking.
ideas.whyMatters: Panic management matters because capitalist markets can require rescue, coordination, and public trust when private confidence collapses.
